## Goal
When an automatic form fails, `WebFormSubmitter._fallback` (`src/freemyid/submitters/web_form.py:400-409`) tells `assisted.todo_for` only "challenge" or "error", so a human step or a missing confirmed listing reads like a crash. Pass the real reason through.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- Reason codes from `submit` (`web_form.py:335-370`): `challenge`, `human_step`, `no_confirmed_listing`, `timeout` (a Playwright or asyncio timeout, matched by exception type name so the test needs no browser), `blocked_by_policy`, `unexpected_page`, `error`.
- `assisted.todo_for` and `_steps` (`src/freemyid/submitters/assisted.py:55-77`, `:155-177`) give each reason one short, calm line of what happened ("The site asked for a step only a person can do."), then today's steps. No reason says "error" or "failed" to the person.
- The `SubmitOutcome.message` code stays `fallback_assisted:<reason>[:<detail>]` with the existing reasons spelled as today, so run reports and in-house tests keep working; new reasons are additions.
- Tests drive `submit` with a fake context whose browser raises each exception type; no real browser starts.

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL).
